issues.description: Weak execution evidence: pov_before_reproduced=false and regressions_ran=0, so the fix's correctness rests on code reasoning rather than demonstrated before/after behavior or a regression suite.

More permissive than the official fix: official rejects a plain file overwriting ANY existing symlink, while ours only rejects when the resolved path escapes the target dir — safe for path traversal but a policy divergence that could let a plain file follow an inside-pointing symlink.

Manual logical resolution of `..` after a followed symlink may diverge from OS physical resolution in exotic layouts; it appears to err toward rejecting escapes but is not identical to kernel semantics.
Larger/more complex than the minimal official fix (40-line helper), increasing maintenance and edge-case surface.

result.root_cause: File#getCanonicalFile() cannot resolve a symlink whose target does not yet exist, so the existing in-directory check can be bypassed by an earlier archive entry that plants a dangling symlink escaping the target dir, through which a later entry then writes.
result.summary: Our patch fixes the vulnerability at the same sink (AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile) as the official fix, adding a manual symlink-resolving canonicalization (Files.isSymbolicLink/readSymbolicLink per segment) that then verifies the resolved path stays under the target directory — the proper CWE-022 defense of record, and arguably broader than the official narrow isSymbolicLink check. It preserves legitimate symlink creation and re-extraction, backed by targeted tests. Confidence is tempered by weak execution evidence (POV did not reproduce pre-patch and zero regressions were run) and a minor policy divergence (it permits plain-file overwrites of symlinks that stay inside the dir, which the official fix blocks outright). Overall a sound, valid alternative fix.
